name: Kotlin
description: Kotlin declarations on the canvas: classes, objects and interfaces of every kind, with properties, functions and supertypes; the properties are reference targets for annotations of other layers.

annotationTypes.name: Class
annotationTypes.description: Regular Kotlin class (class). Use it for types with behavior and state that are not just data: services, repositories, view models, implementations. The modality says whether it can be inherited from (open) or is abstract. Do not confuse it with data class (data with generated equals/copy), object (single instance) and interface. A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up. inner requires Declared in. A companion object is the Object marking (with companion = sim) with Declared in pointing to the owner class.

annotationTypes.name: Data class
annotationTypes.description: Data class: data class with equals, hashCode, copy, toString and componentN generated from the properties of the primary constructor. It needs at least one property in the constructor (declaredIn = construtor). It cannot be abstract, open, sealed or inner. Use it for models, DTOs and immutable UI state (prefer val). Do not confuse it with a regular class (without these methods) or with value class (wraps a single value). A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.

annotationTypes.name: Sealed class
annotationTypes.description: Sealed class: closed, abstract hierarchy; the direct subtypes are known at compile time, which allows an exhaustive when. The subtypes are the mapped declarations whose supertypes points (typeRef) to it; the agent finds them through that reference. Use it for results and states with different shapes. Do not confuse it with enum (fixed instances of the same shape) or with open class (open hierarchy). A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.

annotationTypes.name: Enum class
annotationTypes.description: Enum class: fixed set of constants of the same shape. The constants live in entries (each line is a reference target with the tag kotlin-enum-entry), with optional constructor arguments. It can implement interfaces but not inherit from classes; it has no type parameters. Do not confuse it with sealed class (subtypes with their own data). A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.

annotationTypes.name: Value class
annotationTypes.description: Value class (@JvmInline): wraps a single value with its own type, with no object cost at runtime. It has exactly one property in the primary constructor (always val) and the @JvmInline annotation. It implements interfaces but does not inherit from classes. Use it for ids and units (UserId, Meters). Do not confuse it with data class (several properties, a real object). A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.

annotationTypes.name: Annotation class
annotationTypes.description: Annotation class: declares an annotation (@Audited, @SerialName). The properties are the constructor parameters (always val; allowed types: primitives, String, KClass, enum, another annotation and arrays of them). targets (@Target) and retention (@Retention) say where it applies and how long it exists. It has no body, functions or supertypes. Do not confuse it with using the annotation: an annotation applied to a declaration goes in that declaration's annotations field. A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.

annotationTypes.name: Object
annotationTypes.description: Object: single-instance declaration (singleton), created lazily. With companion = sim it is the companion object, linked to the owner class through the Declared in field (outer); the companion's name is usually Companion. Drawing it inside the owner class is only a visual tidy-up. It can inherit from a class and implement interfaces; it has no constructor or type parameters. Do not confuse it with class (several instances) or with data object (adds readable toString/equals).

annotationTypes.name: Sealed interface
annotationTypes.description: Sealed interface: closed interface; the direct implementors are known at compile time (exhaustive when) and live in the same module and package. The subtypes are the declarations whose supertypes points (typeRef) to it. More flexible than sealed class: the subtypes can be data class, object, data object or enum and can inherit from another class. Do not confuse it with a regular interface (open). A nested declaration (inner, nested, companion) is linked to its outer declaration through the Declared in field (outer); drawing the marking inside the outer one is only an optional visual tidy-up.
